validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/SPEC: real, independently confirmed. Four independent origins agree on the same two headline figures GEM already carries (LengthKnown=1000 mi, Capacity=1000 MMcf/d): (1) Enterprise's own corporate history page ('Acquired Acadian Gas LLC from an affiliate of Shell Oil Company for $244 million in cash. Acadian's assets consist of three Louisiana intrastate pipeline systems with over 1,000 miles of pipeline with a combined capacity of over one billion cubic feet per day'); (2) mergr.com, an independent M&A database, same '1,000 miles ... over one billion cubic feet ... per day', acquisition dated 2000-09-25; (3) Enterprise's own 2010 SEC investor presentation (S-4/425 filing, sec.gov, an independent regulatory filing of the company's own disclosures): 'Three systems - Acadian, Cypress and Evangeline - comprise over 1,000 miles of pipe with throughput capacity of 1 Bcf/d'; (4) Natural Gas Intelligence (naturalgasintel.com, trade press, fully independent of Enterprise), 2000: 'Enterprise Products Partners L.P. has purchased Acadian Gas LLC's extensive southern Louisiana assets, which include 1,000-plus miles of pipeline, more than 1 Bcf/d of capacity ... from Coral Energy LLC for $226 million in cash. Coral Energy ... is an affiliate of Shell Oil Co.' A fifth source, a PHMSA-hosted public-awareness brochure (pipelinesafetyinfo.com, though authored by Enterprise, so not counted as independent) itemizes the umbrella group as four sub-systems (Acadian Gas 654 mi, Cypress Gas 577 mi, Pelican Pipeline 27 mi, Pontchartrain Natural Gas ~2 mi), consistent with the roughly 1,000+ mile combined total GEM's row represents. Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are trivially confirmed by every source describing the system in the present tense as an active natural-gas transport network. validity.researcher_notes: GEM's P0143 carries FuelSource='Haynesville shale field' and StartLocation='Haynesville shale field', but every independent source that supports this row's own Length (1000 mi) and Capacity (1000 MMcf/d) values describes those same figures as belonging to the ORIGINAL system Enterprise acquired from Coral Energy/Shell in September 2000 - eight years before Haynesville shale gas production began (~2008) and nine years before Enterprise/Duncan Energy even announced a Haynesville-directed extension (OGJ, 2009-10-28, https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/17277371/enterprise-duncan-to-expand-acadian-gas-line-into-haynesville-shale - a separate, later pipeline). Enterprise's own 2010 SEC investor presentation (sec.gov, filing 000095012310092582) explicitly geolocates the pre-Haynesville 'Existing Acadian Gas System' as linking 'natural gas from Baton Rouge onshore Louisiana and offshore GOM to industrial, electric and LDC customers in Louisiana' - not Haynesville shale gas. The Haynesville-sourced volumes flow through a physically and administratively separate 270-mile 'Haynesville Extension' pipeline (roster PID P5709), which only entered commercial service in November 2011 per Enterprise's own history page. Because P0143's Length/Capacity match the pre-2009 legacy system rather than the Extension (whose length is 270 mi and capacity is 1,800-2,500 MMcf/d, not 1,000/1,000), the row appears to blend two different eras/pipelines: legacy spec values on a Haynesville-labeled FuelSource/StartLocation. This is a genuine mismatch worth a human review, not a case I can silently overwrite with a fabricated corrected location.

cross_row_leads.facts: Haynesville Extension: 270-mile, 42-inch/36-inch pipeline, ~1.8 Bcf/d capacity (expandable to 2.1 Bcf/d), total project cost ~$1.56 billion, expected in service September 2011. Matches roster's P5709 length (270 mi) and diameter (30,36,42) exactly.

'Commercial operations on the Haynesville Extension of our Acadian Gas system began in November [2011]. This provides ... access to 1.8 Bcf/d of incremental natural gas takeaway capacity.' Then Dec 2021 (Gillis Lateral in-service): capacity increased 1.8->2.1 Bcf/d via added horsepower at the Mansfield Compressor Station, Mansfield, Louisiana. Then May 2023: a further +400 MMcf/d expansion (compression only) raised capacity from 2.1 to 2.5 Bcf/d. Roster's P5709 still shows Capacity=1800 - this appears STALE; current capacity per Enterprise's own 2023 disclosure is 2,500 MMcf/d, not 1,800.

2009-10-28 announcement: Enterprise Products Partners LP and Duncan Energy Partners LP announced plans (via jointly owned Acadian Gas LLC subsidiary) to extend the Louisiana intrastate system into the Haynesville Shale - i.e. this is the original proposal for what became P5709. Candidate ProposalYear=2009.

2023-05-31: Enterprise Products Partners completed a 400-MMcfd expansion of the Acadian Haynesville Extension pipeline, increasing its capacity to 2.5 Bcf/d. Corroborates the capacity-increase figure above from a second, independent (non-Enterprise) origin.

'The 83-mile Gillis Lateral pipeline originates near Alexandria, Louisiana on our Acadian Haynesville Extension system and extends to third party pipeline interconnects near Gillis, Louisiana ... capability to transport approximately 1.0 Bcf/d.' Commercial service started/announced December 2021. Matches roster's P3283 length (83 mi) and capacity (1000 MMcf/d) exactly; candidate StartYear1=2021.

Independent (non-Enterprise) corroboration, dated ~2021: 'an 80-mile lateral from its mainline to terminate in Gillis, Louisiana... a 1 Bcf/d expansion with a net increase to the Acadian system of 300 MMcf/d to 2.1 Bcf/d from 1.8 Bcf/d... Enterprise shows a 4Q2021 in-service date.'

Third independent source, ~Dec 16 2021: Gillis Lateral commercial service start, ~80 mi, ~1 Bcf/d, Mansfield compressor station in DeSoto Parish. Also names Natalie Gayden, Enterprise SVP natural gas assets, as a spokesperson quote if an operator-contact field is ever needed.

This May-2023, 400-MMcfd, compression-only expansion (2.1->2.5 Bcf/d on the Haynesville Extension) is almost certainly what roster P5401 (cap=400, len=0.0, dia blank) represents - the len=0/blank-diameter pairing already correctly reflects GEM's own 'no new physical pipe' convention for a compression-only expansion. Completion date 2023-05-31.
